feedback.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}=\frac{4}{s}+\frac{1}{s-6},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}=\frac{4}{s}-\frac{1}{s-6}.
$$

Find the solution to the original initial value problem.

| $x(t)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | $\,\,+\,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  | $\,\,{e}^{6t}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  | {{field-4}} |  |  |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{1}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{s}+\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}+{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4\cdot 1+{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =4+{e}^{6t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{2}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{s}-\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4\cdot 1-{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =4-{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4+{e}^{6t} \\ 4-{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$
